response.final_text:
**Proposed disposition:** CLOSE_FP, confidence 0.85. It is a proposal only and awaits a human decision (case C-A-261022-0004).

**Three facts that drove it:**
1. The trader is an ALGO on desk ALGO-EXEC. Every order is a PEGGED child of one of two parents, P-T-X1022-04-B and P-T-X1022-04-S. Each is 2889 (the desk's typical size, 1.15x depth) and rests at the touch. Cancels are symmetric (0.997), and no single order reached 3x depth. The detector's "large" trigger came from gross volume built up by constant re-pricing.
2. The order was working. A BUY child filled 267 before the 946 SELL fill. The SELL moved the price against the trader (-2 ticks), with no reversion and a round trip of 0.27 ticks. That is no benefit from the opposite-side trade, and there were no repetitions.
3. There was no market event, no risk event and no prior alerts on this trader. Order-to-trade ratio is 44.7 against a typical 25.0. I attribute that to the pegged re-pricing.

**What would change my mind:** evidence that the pegged children had no genuine parent order. Or evidence that the 946 SELL was made at a price the one-sided displayed size had moved in the trader's favour, with reversion after the cancel.
